query: What signals suggest a goal will be highly achieved?

per_column.name: goal_outcome_type
per_column.rationale: A meaningful grouping axis for comparing achievement by outcome, though it closely tracks the existing category column, limiting novelty. Values match description/category cleanly across all samples.

per_column.name: metric_alignment_clarity
per_column.rationale: Highly relevant to the query: whether the tracking metric matches the goal is a plausible driver of achievement. Judgments are well grounded (e.g., Expense Ratio for customer satisfaction correctly flagged as proxy/misaligned; Employee Turnover for satisfaction as misaligned), a warranted inference from metric vs description.

per_column.name: implementation_mechanism_type
per_column.rationale: Gives a genuine new axis (how the goal is pursued) to model achievement. Mechanisms are reasonably read from descriptions (resource optimization, behavioral change, process redesign, training), with only mild interpretive latitude.

per_column.name: goal_scope_span
per_column.rationale: Scope/breadth is a sensible signal for achievability. Sample rows are all single_initiative, plausibly grounded, though distinguishing multi_department/enterprise_wide from often-terse text carries some inference risk not verifiable here.

per_column.name: timeline_horizon
per_column.rationale: Time horizon is a strong candidate signal for achievement and gives a good grouping axis. Values largely match textual cues (Q4->quarter, next fiscal year->fiscal_year), though 'upcoming year' mapped to multi_year is a mild overreach; NULLs for silent rows are acceptable.

per_column.name: financial_quantification_present
per_column.rationale: A binary presence flag is useful for distinguishing quantified financial goals but is coarse. Some readings look generous: a customer satisfaction 78%->90% goal marked True for financial quantification is questionable, since the percentages are non-financial, slightly undermining groundedness.

judge.rationale: The added columns supply several genuine, query-relevant axes (metric alignment, mechanism, scope, horizon) that let an analyst group and model goal achievement, going well beyond the original fields. Values are mostly sound readings of the description/metric/category text. Minor groundedness concerns include a broad 'financial_quantification_present' flag firing on non-financial percentage targets and an occasional horizon overreach ('upcoming year'->multi_year), but no systematic invention of facts. goal_outcome_type is somewhat redundant with the existing category column, capping its usefulness.
